name: gitea
description: Self-hosted Git service with repositories, issues, pull requests, packages, and team collaboration

fields.name: WEB_PORT
fields.label: R1: Web Interface Port
fields.help: Host port used to open Gitea in bridge mode. In Host Mode, Gitea listens directly on NAS port 3000.

fields.name: SSH_PORT
fields.label: R2: Git SSH Port
fields.help: Host port used for Git-over-SSH clone and push operations. This value is also advertised in Gitea's SSH clone URLs. If you select Host Mode, use 22 unless Gitea's internal SSH listener is separately reconfigured.

fields.name: DATA_LOCATION
fields.label: R3: Data Folder
fields.help: Bind-mounted folder containing Gitea's configuration, repositories, SQLite database, packages, logs, and other persistent data. The selected UID and GID must be able to write here.

fields.name: PUID
fields.label: R4: PUID
fields.help: User ID used by Gitea for bind-mounted file permissions. EasyDocker fills this from your saved PUID persistent variable; it should match the owner of the data folder on your NAS.

fields.name: PGID
fields.label: R5: PGID
fields.help: Group ID used by Gitea for bind-mounted file permissions. EasyDocker fills this from your saved PGID persistent variable; it should match the group that owns the data folder on your NAS.

fields.name: TZ
fields.label: O1: Time Zone
fields.help: IANA time zone used for container timestamps, for example Asia/Dubai, Europe/London, or America/New_York.

fields.name: GITEA_ROOT_URL
fields.label: O2: Site URL
fields.help: Optional canonical URL used in links and redirects. Leave blank for initial local setup. If Gitea is accessed through a reverse proxy, enter the complete public address, such as https://git.example.com/. For direct NAS access you may use http://NAS-IP:3000/.

fields.name: GITEA_NETWORK_MODE
fields.label: O3: Network
fields.help: Choose Create New Bridge for the recommended default, Host Mode, or an existing named Docker network. Bridge mode keeps the configurable web and SSH port mappings.

fields.name: RESTART_POLICY
fields.label: O4: Restart Policy
fields.help: Controls whether the container restarts automatically.

fields.name: GITEA_IMAGE
fields.label: A1: Image
fields.help: Official stable Gitea image. For predictable upgrades, advanced users may replace latest with a specific release tag.

fields.name: GITEA_WEB_PORT_MAPPING
fields.label: A2: Bridge Web Port Mapping
fields.help: Automatically generated for bridge or an existing Docker network and removed in Host Mode.

fields.name: GITEA_SSH_PORT_MAPPING
fields.label: A3: Bridge SSH Port Mapping
fields.help: Automatically generated Git SSH mapping for bridge or an existing Docker network and removed in Host Mode.

fields.name: GITEA_CONTAINER_NAME
fields.label: Container Name
fields.help: EasyDocker sets the container name from the project name.

fields.name: GITEA_DATA_TARGET
fields.label: Internal Data Folder
fields.help: Official persistent data location inside the Gitea container.

fields.name: GITEA_INTERNAL_WEB_PORT
fields.label: Internal Web Port
fields.help: Recipe-managed Gitea web port inside the container.

fields.name: GITEA_INTERNAL_SSH_PORT
fields.label: Internal SSH Port
fields.help: Recipe-managed Gitea SSH port inside the container.

ui.overview: Gitea is a lightweight self-hosted Git platform with repository hosting, issues, pull requests, releases, packages, and collaboration features.
what_happens: One Gitea container will be created using its built-in SQLite database
Configuration, repositories, database files, packages, and logs will persist in the selected bind-mounted data folder
The web interface will be available on the selected web port
Git-over-SSH will be available on the selected SSH port and that port will appear in SSH clone URLs
Bridge networking is selected by default, with Host Mode and existing Docker networks also available
On first launch, open the web interface and complete Gitea's installation wizard to create the administrator account
ui.data_location: The selected data folder contains the complete Gitea installation, including its SQLite database, configuration, repositories, attachments, packages, and logs. Back up the entire folder before upgrades or migrations.
